q: Are the Exercise Science programs the same programs previously offered at California University (CalU)?
a: 100% the same. PennWest was formed by integrating three historic universities. The academic programs that were offered at CalU are the same degree programs with the same faculty at PennWest. Basically, we now offer the same nationally respected exercise science degree programs with all the advantages of a larger, more efficient university. It’s a true “win-win-win”! A win for our students, a win for our faculty, and a win for our university. We have also offered a fully online bachelor’s degree in Exercise Science since 2005.

q: How old is PennWest University?
a: PennWest may be a new name, but its history spans nearly 165 years of tradition and academic excellence.  Formed by the integration of California, Clarion and Edinboro universities, PennWest is a model for future success. It’s building on the strengths of each university to offer every student a richer experience, while holding down the cost of education. Click here to explore our PennWest Fast facts Three brick-and-mortar campuses welcome residential as well as commuter students, and its online degrees allow you to choose the academic and personal options that suit you best.

q: Where is PennWest University located?
a: PennWest University is located in western Pennsylvania and is the second largest university on the western side of Pennsylvania. With three main campuses located in the towns of California, Clarion, and Edinboro Pennsylvania, the university offers several on campus degree programs. The PennWest Global Online campus, available to students across the country and around the world, offers challenging, well-respected degrees from a state university at an affordable cost.

q: How many students attend PennWest University?
a: The total enrollment at PennWest University hovers around 10,000 students. PennWest is a medium sized university, with over 190,000 living alumni.

q: What are the admissions requirements?
a: Applicants should have a Bachelor’s Degree from a Regionally accredited institution with a final Grade Point Average of 3.0 or higher. However, those with GPA’s under 3.0 are encouraged to apply and may be granted Conditional Admission into the program (with financial aid eligibility).

a: Yes, all courses required for the program are offered fully online. No need to ever travel to campus.

q: How do I submit my application materials?

q: Who are the faculty?
a: Our faculty are leaders in the field of exercise science. Our faculty include Hall of Famers, business owners, Journal Editors, Master Trainers, and many other impressive titles. We are fortunate to have several tenured professors teaching in our program and a wealth of adjunct professors from around the country who are experts in their field. A brief description of our faculty is included below: 12 Full-time faculty dedicated to teach online courses 100% of full time faculty have terminal academic or clinical degrees (PhD, EdD, DPT, OTD) 100% of faculty have specialty degree credentials (ATC, Ex Phys, OT, PT, CSCS) All faculty have worked clinically from which to extract true experiential teaching All faculty have completed the required online preparation courses that prepare them to use technology to teach in an online environment

q: Have the faculty been trained to teach in an online classroom?

Our faculty are very qualified to teach in an online environment and most of them only teach online. Our faculty work with PennWest Global Online Instructional Designers to create the best courses we can offer to our students.

q: Can I work full time while enrolled in the program?
a: Yes. Most of our students work full time while enrolled in the program. In fact, many of our students are very busy professionals who can balance their schoolwork with family and work obligations. Our exercise science degree program was created for busy people with the goal of offering a high quality, challenging curriculum while making sure the program is not too overwhelming for our students.

q: Are GREs required for admission?
a: GREs are not required. We feel we can learn about you as a professional from your application versus observing a score on a standardized test.

q: Does PennWest accept transfer credits?
a: Yes! We welcome transfer credits. Transfer credits must be graduate level when transferring into the master’s in exercise science and health promotion degree.  Click here to complete the Transfer Credit Request Form.

q: Does PennWest accept professional experience towards course credits?
a: Yes! We welcome Prior Learning Assessment (PLA) credits. PLA credits that are approved will be used in place of course credit in the master’s in exercise science and health promotion degree. We try very hard to save you time and money by giving you credit for your hard work and professional experience.

q: How long is the program?
a: The program can be completed in as little as 12 months with students taking courses in fall, winter, spring, and summer terms. However, we are very flexible with course sequences and can arrange a part time program or extended course sequence, which allows a student to complete the program in 18 months or more.

q: What program options are available?
a: We offer six single focus areas in the Masters of Exercise Science and Health Promotion (ESHP) degree. You can choose any single area OR choose two or more areas (only adding an additional six credits for each area). Click here to find out more about our degree options. The six focus areas are: Nutrition Sport Performance Enhancement and Injury Prevention Rehabilitation Science Sport Psychology Tactical Strength and Conditioning Wellness and Fitness

q: Can I enroll part-time?
a: At PennWest, we are very flexible with course sequences and can arrange a part time program or extended course sequence, which allows a student to complete the exercise science master’s degree program in 18 months or more.

q: Is there a residency required?
a: No. All courses required for the program are offered fully online. No need to ever travel to campus.

q: Is a thesis required?
a: No. As an applied master’s degree that teaches you “real-world” information, we do not require a thesis. However, all the information you will learn is based on evidence-based research. You will enroll in a research course that require you to complete a research paper focused on a topic of your choice. For students who want an enhanced research experience, we do offer an optional Research Project course in the Exercise Science program.

a: All National Academy of Sports Medicine (NASM) and National Association of Speed & Explosion (NASE) educational content is already embedded in our courses. q: How many hours per week are required to be successful in the program?
a: On average, most students will spend between 8-10 hours per week interacting in the courses, learning the material, and completing assignments. Some weeks may be a little lighter and some a little more demanding.

q: How many courses will I take each semester?
a: The typical number of courses you will take in a given term is two-three courses. No need to worry, we have had thousands of students over the past twenty years take three courses in a term and do just fine. Our goal, like yours, is for you to succeed.

q: Does PennWest University offer a doctorate program in Exercise Science?

q: Does PennWest University offer a bachelors program in Exercise Science?

q: How many students are accepted into a cohort?
a: A typical cohort in a given start term would be 30 students. Our goal is to keep course numbers at a reasonable amount so you can experience the highest quality education possible.

q: Do I have to “log-in” on certain days of the week?
a: No, our programs are asynchronous which means there is never a specific day and time to login. Most of our course units open on a Monday and require that you complete the work for that unit by the following Sunday. In other words, our courses allow YOU to decide when to log in to stay on top of your coursework. Whatever day and time works best for you, the busy professional.

q: Can I receive financial aid?

a: Billing occurs prior to each semester and is communicated through each student’s myPennWest portal online. The University does not mail paper invoices to enrolled students. For winter and summer terms, invoices are made available approximately 10 days prior to the term start. For detailed information on the Student Billing process, please visit https://my.pennwest.edu/billing.
